I am PhD student of human resource management in Iran.I defensed my thesis in tittle the effect of cognitive emotion regulation on work-related subjective well-being and work behavior. I used multidimensional IRT in order to analyze my data .i used Mirt Package which is designed by you and i really appreciate your hard working and your effort in order to development knowledge in this field. I understood  and used you package but i have some problem .could you please help me?

First of all, i don't know haw we can judge about difficulty ? I didn't fine a cut of for judging difficulty throw books and paper.

Difficulty is determined based on the values of the intercept parameters. Higher intercept values indicate an item is generally easier to endorse. You could also use itemplot() or plot(model, type = 'trace') to visualize the different difficulties, if that helps.

Second how we can judge about dimensions? if the literature support that ,for example cognitive emotion regulation divided in to two main dimension which are named adjusted strategies and unadjusted strategies. Can we use exploratory factor with presumption of 2 factor In mirt Package?

Yes you can use exploratory item factor analysis in mirt by specifing your model as a numeric input, such as mirt(data, model = 2). The results will need to be rotated in the same way as exploratory factor analysis though. If you have more specific hypothesis to test, try looking into the ?mirt.model documentation to specify a more specific pattern of loadings.
can we use regression or correlation between scores in order to test our Hypothesis?

I'm unsure what this means, sorry.
